fix(console): print gives a container lines of its own, as Rich does (rich-console-5k3)

A container argument (array, typed array, Map, Set, or an object without its
own toString — Pretty's `isExpandable`, Rich's `is_expandable`) is now a block
in `Console.print`, like any renderable: `print("a", { x: 1 }, "b")` prints
three lines, as Rich fc41075a does. Scalars still join the text run.

`isExpandable` is the one definition of "container": `_shape` reads its text
arm from it, so print and Pretty cannot disagree.

feat(template-bindings)!: declare arity for go-template-js 0.10.0 (#224)

* feat(template-bindings): declare arity on every binding

go-template-js 0.10.0 requires every TemplateFunc to declare its arity and
refuses a wrong argument count at the gate, so the bodies' own count checks
(ramp's value/easing/stop minimum, asAmount's undefined arm) are deleted.

* test(template-bindings): a body's error arrives as the engine's call-site error

go-template-js reports a function body's error as Go does — error calling
<name>: <err> — with the body's error as its cause, and refuses a
fractional integer argument as Go words it.

* chore(deps): go-template-js 0.10.0; release 0.18.0

* fix(template-bindings): one-line renderTemplate error; drop dead int-slot check; pin style arity

Review of #224: renderTemplate formats an engine error by its one-line
message (String(e) now carries the 0.10 code frame); darken/lighten drop
the finite check their int slot already guarantees; docs name the whole-
number level; every style arity declaration site is pinned by a test.

fix(columns): lay out as Rich's grid, so padding and expand take effect (rich-columns-awe, rich-columns-sf4)

`padding` was never read and `expand` was stored and never read: the gutter
was a hard-coded 2 and every layout divided the whole offer among uniform
columns, so there was nothing left for `expand` to do.

Columns now decides what Rich's `Table.grid(collapse_padding, pad_edge=False)`
decides: a column count found by Rich's search, each column as wide as its own
widest item, a gap of the wider horizontal padding side, rows separated by
`top + max(0, top - bottom)`, and `expand` spreading the surplus with a port of
`ratio_distribute`. Items render with a default Column's options (left,
ellipsis). Output is byte-identical to Rich 9d8f9a3 for every case pinned in the
tests and for the docs listing.

One departure, where Rich has no sound answer: a declared `width` searches the
column count the same way instead of `max_width // (width + gap)`, so it never
lays out empty trailing columns (sf4) and never divides by zero.
